en: The Philippine eagle, our national bird, has a massive wingspan of up to two meters, making it one of the largest forest eagles globally.
The Philippine flag features exactly eight rays on its sun, representing the first eight provinces that revolted against Spanish colonial rule in 1896.
The Philippine Senate consists of exactly 24 elected members, while the House of Representatives has over 300 members depending on the district population.
The Philippines is highly multilingual, with linguists identifying over 180 distinct living languages spoken across its more than 7,000 islands.
National hero Jose Rizal was a polymath who could speak and write in at least 22 different languages during his lifetime.
The Panagbenga Flower Festival in Baguio City typically lasts for exactly one month, celebrating the blooming of flowers with massive street parades.
The famous Ifugao Rice Terraces, built by indigenous peoples over 2,000 years ago, stretch for hundreds of kilometers and reach up to 1,500 meters above sea level.
The Philippines is divided into 81 provinces, which are further subdivided into over 1,400 municipalities and nearly 42,000 barangays for local governance.
National Scientist Fe del Mundo practiced medicine for over 60 years and invented a bamboo incubator that maintains a constant 37 degrees Celsius.
The Philippine basic education system requires exactly 13 years of schooling, comprising one year of kindergarten, six of elementary, and six of high school.
Arnis, the national martial art and sport, incorporates over 100 different striking and blocking techniques using sticks, knives, and bare hands.
The Philippine national anthem, Lupang Hinirang, was originally composed as an instrumental march in 1898, with its official Filipino lyrics added 59 years later in 1957.
